prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a general, ligand-controlled method that made aryl amines, which are ubiquitous in drugs, agrochemicals and materials, accessible under predictable conditions. It changed retrosynthetic thinking, since an aryl C-N bond is now an ordinary disconnection, and it is used daily at industrial scale. Buchwald and Hartwig independently established the catalytic version in the mid-1990s and then drove the successive ligand generations (biaryl phosphines, hindered alkyl phosphines and ferrocenyl ligands), so attribution is a clean pair. The chemistry has been reproduced for 25+ years, so the maturity question is settled. Among the shortlisted candidates it is the one with the least uncertainty on all three criteria: originality, attribution and maturity.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is the 2010 prize for Pd-catalysed cross-coupling (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki). Some members will see C-N coupling as an extension of that prize, not a separate discovery. There is also the Kosugi and Migita tin-amide precedent, which a citation must treat carefully. Finally, the candidate has weaker headline appeal than newer, more fashionable fields, and it leads in none of the opening tallies.

responses.point: Chabes ranked B032 third and called the impact undisputed, but worried that the 2010 cross-coupling prize may already be seen as covering it. He also flagged credit for the Kosugi and Migita precursors.
responses.response: I take the 2010 concern seriously but think it misreads the chemistry. The 2010 prize rewarded C-C bond formation through well-behaved organometallic partners. C-N coupling needed a separate solution: amido-palladium intermediates prone to beta-hydride elimination and slow C-N reductive elimination, which were only overcome by the ligand design of Buchwald and Hartwig. That is a new mechanistic problem and not an extension. Kosugi's tin amides were stoichiometric in tin and narrow in scope, so I think a citation worded around the catalytic, general amination answers the precursor issue without adding a third laureate.

responses.point: Linke, our chair, ranked B031 (sequencing-by-synthesis) first, argued the core is chemistry in nucleotide design and surface attachment, and ranked B032 only fifth. He also noted that credit among Ju, Mayer and Rothberg is contested and commercially entangled.
responses.response: I agree the Solexa chemistry is a real invention and I ranked B031 fifth myself. My difficulty is the one Linke raises: with Ju, Mayer and Rothberg all having strong parallel claims, any pair or trio will be contested, and it also invites the question of whether this is chemistry or physiology/medicine. For B032 the attribution is far cleaner. I would not oppose B031 as a fallback, but I would want that attribution debate settled before it ranks above a method whose credit is not in doubt.

responses.point: Aili ranked B063 (targeted protein degradation) first, arguing it turns small molecules into programmable effectors of ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis, a new modality with large therapeutic momentum. He also accepted that credit is spread over Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and others.
responses.response: The concept is original, and I ranked B063 fourth for that reason. I disagree with Aili on timing and attribution. No degrader is approved yet, so the clinical validation is incomplete. A three-person cut must separate PROTAC design (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) from the cereblon and molecular-glue mechanism (Handa, Ito), which are really two stories. Much of the strength of the case is the promise of the modality and not what it has so far demonstrated. A discovery with 25 years of use should not rank below one whose largest claims are still prospective. I would revisit this once someone shows how a coherent citation and three names can be drawn.

responses.point: Sparr ranked B035 (ionizable lipid nanoparticles) first, as a deliverable medicine platform built on lipid self-assembly and bilayer phase behaviour, while noting that credit is split between the Vancouver group and the Anderson and Langer lipidoid line.
responses.response: I accept that this is a clear and important molecular-design achievement and that the lipid physical chemistry is real, which I am less qualified than Sparr to judge. My reservations are practical. The credit is unresolved among six names, partly entangled with patent disputes, and the practical impact has already been recognised in the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA vaccines. If the committee goes this way I would want a very narrow citation on ionizable-lipid design, but I cannot yet support it over a candidate with a clean three-way fit of discovery, credit and maturity.

uncertainties: Whether a majority will treat C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize or as an extension of it.
Whether the citation needs to acknowledge the Kosugi and Migita precursor work, and how.
Whether the group would prefer a two-part prize, since only one extra person could be added to the two C-N laureates within the three-person limit.
Photoredox catalysis and C-H functionalization, which I ranked second and third, are not on the shortlist, so I cannot argue for them here.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I have no known collaboration, mentorship or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or the other shortlisted candidates. My own field is synthetic organic methodology, so I should be read as having a field bias toward B032.
